text: For this activity, you will need two pieces of paper and two things to write with (ideally two different colours).

What to do:

  1. Line 1
    Write the beginning of a sentence starting with ‘If’. Don’t put a full stop – the other person is going to finish your sentence. Instead, finish with a comma.
    e.g. 'If the world was made of custard',
    Fold the paper over to hide your writing.
  2. Line 2
    Swap paper (don’t look at what the other person wrote).
    Write something to finish off the hidden sentence – write it like this ‘something would/should/will/could __________’e.g.:
    • a hare will dig a hole.
    • cake would be well cooked.
    • Grandma will sneeze.
  3. Line 3
    Keeping the same piece of paper, on a new line, use the words you just wrote to start a new ‘If’ sentence (ending with a comma).
    e.g. you wrote ‘Grandma will sneeze’ so now you write ‘If Grandma sneezes’.
    Fold the paper over to hide your writing.
  4. Line 4
    Swap with the other person and again write something to finish the sentence.
  5. Line 5
    Again, Keeping the same piece of paper, on a new line, use the words you just wrote to start a new ‘If’ sentence.
  6. Lines 6+
    After 3 or 4 sentences, unravel the paper and have a look!
